summary: Streaming response jitter followed by silent SSE/WebSocket disconnect during long chat generation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer on Dedicated capacity reports that long chat sessions (5k+ token prompts) over SSE and WebSocket begin with normal streaming but after a period of elevated per-token latency (~300-600ms) the stream goes silent and the client observes a silent disconnect (no error frame) or abrupt close.

Impact:
- A single customer (Acme Health, dedicated) experiencing frequent user-facing interruptions in long interactive sessions across multiple regions.
- Estimated 20% of long sessions (>2000 tokens) affected during observed burst window.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-03) backed by redwood-13b-v1 workers.
- Fronting: Envoy edge -> NGINX LB -> internal API gateway -> serving-runtime.
- Observed regions: prod-us-east primary, affected sessions also seen proxied from eu-west clients.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Create a long chat prompt (instructions + 4 large context chunks; target output >3k tokens).
2) Open SSE subscription to /v1/chat/stream using customer API key and stream response.
3) After ~60-120s into generation, client reports heartbeat missing then connection close without explicit 5xx or 4xx.
4) Replays show same behavior roughly 1 in 5 attempts under burst load.

Observed logs & artifacts:
- Envoy edge logs show a 200 response for the request with a final FIN from client side shortly after a prolonged period of bytes silence. No application-level 5xx recorded.
- NGINX access log excerpt: "GET /v1/chat/stream 200 0.123 - - -" followed by upstream_disconnect 
- Runtime stdout capture for worker: repeated "token-latency=0.45s" spikes and then worker reports "client closed connection".
- Client tcp dump (provided) shows keepalive window with no SSE comment lines for ~40s, then TCP RST from client agent.

Hypothesis (initial):
- Upstream proxy (NGINX) or intermediate idle timeout is closing connections after a threshold when streaming output is delayed due to transient model token-latency spikes (KV cache warm/thaw or kernel swap).
- Alternatively, when the serving-runtime pauses worker emission (prefetch/backpressure or kernel swap for quantized worker), Envoy/NGINX may not see periodic bytes and assume idle connection, closing it silently.
- There is also evidence of increased queuing at the router during autoscaling events which aligns with timestamps of affected sessions.

Notes:
- Customer reproduced against both SSE and WebSocket protocols; behavior is protocol-agnostic.
- Affected sessions often include model fallback events during which the server swaps a worker (observed canary-to-main fallback), which correlates with the silent period.

Attachments referenced:
- pcap: acme_health_sse_2026-03-12.pcap (attached to ticket)
- runtime traces: trace-2026-03-12-14-01.log
- dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/streaming/latency?range=2026-03-12

investigation_notes: Confirmed: behavior reproduces in lab when inducing token-latency spikes (artificial sleep in runtime emission path).
Envoy front door keeps connection open beyond 60s when periodic bytes are sent; NGINX upstream_read_timeout at 30s causes internal upstream disconnect when no bytes seen for that period.

Worker logs show KV cache migration events and occasional kernel swap for quantized workers at times that align with customer reports. These operations can pause emission for tens of seconds depending on sequence length and device warmup.

Autoscaler events: brief worker eviction/creation observed in dedicated pool at 2026-03-12T08:03Z which aligns with an uptick in incidents. Suggests combined effect: transient model warm + aggressive LB timeout -> client disconnects.
Heartbeat emission experiment indicates that keeping periodic zero-byte comments or tiny SSE comments prevents the proxy from closing the connection.
resolution:
Mitigations applied: 1) Temporarily increased NGINX upstream_read_timeout to 90s for affected dedicated pools (rolled 2026-03-14 11:45 UTC). 2) Deployed runtime feature flag to emit configurable SSE comment heartbeats every 15s during long generations to survive proxy idle windows. 3) Created follow-up task for runtime team to reduce kernel-swap pause durations and improve warm worker handoff (see linked PR).

Next steps / permanent fix:
- Runtime: optimize KV cache migration path and make worker warmups non-blocking (owner: Elena Gomez, ETA: 2 weeks).
- Infra: review and align idle timeout semantics between Envoy/NGINX across clusters (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA: 1 week).
- Product: update docs and SDKs to recommend client keepalive options and surface guidance for long streaming sessions (owner: Priya Menon, ETA: 3 weeks).
